sentence: This project provides tissue studies and strength tests of bone in mice and humans to help study diseases of the skeleton.
This project measures pollutant chemicals such as metals and hydrocarbons in biological and environmental samples to help study how exposure affects development.
This project studies genomics, transcriptomics and proteomics data from human tumors to find changes linked to cancer.
This project provides fluorescence microscopy instruments and image analysis software for cancer research.
This project builds biosensors that visualize histone methylations and chromatin structures in single cells during embryonic differentiation.
This project studies how repeated trauma changes activity and gene function in the hippocampus and tests a neurosteroid treatment.
This project tries to find out which proteins syndecan-4 works with inside muscle stem cells to direct muscle regeneration.
This project studies the neural circuits that produce activity in dopamine neurons, which are linked to several psychiatric disorders.
This project studies why RNA variants exist and how they are regulated and work, using experiments and computer analysis.
This project maps gene activity in single Plasmodium falciparum parasites to find what controls sexual differentiation during gametocyte development.
This project studies how antibiotic synthesis genes in a tick endosymbiont are regulated near pathogenic Rickettsia and tries to identify their products.
This project studies why some leukemia cells depend on an RNA binding protein that regulates alternative RNA splicing.
This project develops a microfluidic chip to load cryoprotective agents into immune cells so they can be preserved and stored.
This project studies how a protein that removes methyl groups from histones controls osteoclasts and bone loss in periodontal disease.
This project tests a low cost mobile microendoscope with artificial intelligence for detecting esophageal cancer.
This project studies how genome integrity, signaling and epigenetic mechanisms drive cancer development and progression.
This project studies how epigenetic changes in macrophage transcriptional factors and effectors affect immune function in sepsis.
This project studies why some cancers need a chromatin remodeler complex to survive and develops small-molecule modulators of it.
This project gives biostatistics, bioinformatics and data management support to cancer prevention research.
This project builds fast variational methods for phylogenetic trees so viral genomic information can be analyzed with machine learning.
